A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRG-SAPPHIRE study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching of retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original MIMIC-IV experiments, training and ablation studies, and physician ratings of model reasoning across 30 cases.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds component-error analysis, physician classification of 100 failures, and evaluation on an institutional dataset.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-7B SFT–GRPO pipeline, algorithmic variants, and final configuration are retained. Completing reward documentation does not establish a changed procedure: v1 already mentions the dense reward's −0.5 value in Appendix A.6.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds evaluation on 2,500 cases from a healthcare institution's internal dataset. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's MIMIC-IV-only evaluation to another clinical data source, while retaining the DRG coding task.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same DRG-LLaMA, ClinicalBERT, CAML, GPT-4o, o3-mini, and R1-Distill-Qwen-32B comparators. Tables 1–2 retain their comparison configurations. The new institutional evaluation reports DRG-SAPPHIRE alone; borrowing DRG-LLaMA's error taxonomy does not add a baseline comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols select common failures across three checkpoints, randomly sample 100 failures for physician review, and match the institutional sample's DRG frequencies to MIMIC. Appendix C.3 also reports early stopping for 50%-SFT runs, qualifying the general one-epoch account without establishing reruns. Existing splits and metrics remain.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces systematic failure analysis absent from v1: component errors across training stages on 9,537 consistently misclassified cases, and physician categorization of 100 final-model failures. These examine whether persistent errors become less severe and which failure types dominate. Existing ablations and illustrative outputs remain.

E5.justification: Pass@1 remains averaged over eight generations, and Figure 12 retains standard-deviation error bars across eight runs. V2 adds no new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds 53.6% accuracy on the institutional cohort, stagewise component-error percentages in Table 3, and physician error frequencies in Table 4, including 32% base-DRG selection errors and 25% CC/MCC errors. Existing Tables 1–2 and the 54.8% MIMIC result are unchanged. The institutional score is a different-dataset result, not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 completes the dense and balanced piecewise reward definitions with −0.5 for a valid DRG having no partial match, a branch missing from v1's formulas. This is a limited formal-definition correction; the GRPO derivations and other mathematical formulations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim state-of-the-art DRG accuracy with physician-validated explanations, approximately logarithmic scaling with SFT data, and limited benefits from scaling RL without sufficient prior knowledge infusion. V2 expands the conclusion's framing but retains these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a substantive deployment qualification: automated billing requires extremely low error rates, whereas operational or educational tools may tolerate more errors. Appendix C.4 interprets component-error reductions as becoming 'less wrong.' Existing mechanism explanations and limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3 and AdamW for SFT. V2 also completes reward documentation and discloses early stopping for the 50%-SFT experiments. These improve implementation transparency without demonstrating that the underlying optimizer or existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of whether RL creates new capabilities, including Ma et al.'s interleaved fine-tuning work. New Appendix E discusses Mu et al.'s hybrid rewards and Sun et al.'s symbolic clinical grounding. AdamW and DeepSpeed references are also added; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes local wording and cross-reference corrections, changes the erroneous 'multilabel' description to 'multi-class,' expands the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments and updated affiliations. Appendix subsections are added and subsequent sections renumbered, while the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3–4, revises several captions, and reflows surrounding material. Figure 5's caption corrects Maj@1 to Maj@8. Existing figures and Tables 1–2 retain their substantive visual organization, without a major redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful institutional evaluation, failure characterization, implementation details, and deployment qualifications. However, new Table 3 has an unexplained inconsistency: the final model's 74.9% principal-diagnosis errors, 62.7% CC/MCC errors, and 33.6% both-wrong rate imply a 104.0% union under a common denominator. Different denominators or definitions are not specified. This unresolved reliability problem in the added evidence prevents a confident net quality judgment.
